text:
zoe-peopleops: Hi — lost my physical insurance card while traveling and need to go to an urgent care in SF tonight. Provider is asking for proof of coverage. What's the fastest way to show them coverage and confirm they're in-network?

benefits-bot: Quick options: 1) Use the digital ID on the carrier app or portal (fastest). 2) Print or screenshot the carrier member card from https://benefits.redwood.com/portal -> My Benefits -> ID Card. 3) If provider needs verification, call carrier provider services at 1-800-555-0199 and ask for immediate eligibility verification for dates of service. Keep the member ID, group number, and DOB.

miguel: If urgent care needs the provider network status, ask them to call the provider line OR give us the clinic name and address and we can check network in the portal for you. Sometimes urgent cares are in-network as part of larger chains.

zoe-peopleops: Clinic name: CityUrgent Care SoMa, 123 Mission St. If you can confirm that would be great — they're asking about co-pay and if PCP referral required.

andrew-hr: I ran a quick lookup — CityUrgent Care SoMa (Tax ID 12-3456789) shows as in-network for our base PPO plan. Copay should be $25 for urgent care; no PCP referral needed. Miguel — can you DM the screenshot of the eligibility page so Zoe can show it?

miguel: Sending DM with screenshot now. Also attached the member digital card PDF. If the clinic still insists, call the provider line and ask them to verify eligibility under group REDWOOD-GRP-01 for member ID X123456.

zoe-peopleops: Got the screenshot and PDF, thank you! They accepted it and billed the $25 copay. Saved the call number in case anything posts incorrectly. Appreciate the quick help :raised_hands:

benefits-bot: Note: if the provider later sends a claim that shows out-of-network, save the EOB and open an appeal within 90 days. Email benefits@redwood.com and include the claim number.
